subject: distsamp function formating data for no detections

messages.author: 732a31c2f861aaca
messages.subject: distsamp function formating data for no detections
parts:
I am using the distsamp function to estimate density using point
counts along a transect. I was hoping for clarification on how the
data should be formatted for this function. I am importing the
detections for each individual as described on the documentation page
for this function.
I then added transects on which no individuals were detected. I run
the model successfully but the estimates are too high so I then
imported the data using each point count as an individual transect and
account for no detections by point instead of by transect , when I do
this the estimates are much more reasonable. I was thinking that when
transects are accounted for when there are no detections it doesn’t
include the number of points within a transect (there could be up to
16 points per transect) the species was not detected on, which
inflates the density estimate. I would appreciate any feedback on the
correct way to format the data.
Here is a summary of the model without including each point the
species was not detected on and is reflected in the Number of sites.
distsamp(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = ovenptUMFv2d, keyfun = "halfnorm",
output = "density", unitsOut = "kmsq")

Density (log-scale):
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
5.01 0.144 34.7 1.11e-263

Detection (log-scale):

3.67 0.0557 66 0

AIC: 630.9878
Number of sites: 73
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 41
Bootstrap iterations: 0

Here is a summary of the model including each point the species was
not detected on.

output = "density", unitsOut = "kmsq")

thanks,
Rob

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] distsamp function formating data for no detections
parts:
Hi Rob,

In the distance sampling literature, a survey point is called a "point transect" as opposed to a "line transect." In your case, you have "point transects" located along a "line transect!" For the purposes of formatting your data for distsamp, ignore the fact that points are on a line. Treat each point as a "point transect" as you did in your second example.

Hope that clears things up.

Richard
